dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "17 annual plans were posted on May 31 by exactly 2 dealers"
"The batch reconciled perfectly (cash matched ledger, all rows accepted)"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "Original transaction dates (May 1-28) were correctly preserved"
"The month-end cluster is a known, permitted operational behavior per the operations email"

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "We are relying on the operations email claim that the dealer contract permits this batching. We do not have the physical contract."
"We cannot confirm if these 17 annual subscribers are genuine or fabricated by the dealer to hit month-end quotas."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Pull a sample of the 17 subscribers and verify their set-top box activation or service usage in May"
"which rules out quota manipulation"

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "No material issue. The cluster reflects a valid, contracted monthly batch submission of annual renewals by specific dealers."
"Safe Next Action"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Contracts allow these dealers to submit annual renewals in a month-end batch" is supported only by an operations email, not the underlying contracts; the submission itself acknowledges that the contracts were not verified.

"Pipeline Defect / Manipulated Reporting: Rejected" is too broad. Accepted rows, unique source event IDs, and cash reconciliation address duplicate and ingestion/reconciliation concerns but do not by themselves exclude every pipeline defect or reporting manipulation.

"which rules out quota manipulation" overstates what a sample of activation or usage logs can establish; it could provide corroboration but cannot fully rule out fabricated customers or other forms of manipulation.

"Subscribers in the batch have no other renewals on record" is not sufficiently reproducible because no query, join keys, date window, or row-level evidence is provided. The claim also does not by itself prove the absence of duplicate cash or entitlement effects.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission handled the main alternatives of duplicate revenue, manipulation, and an ingestion problem, and identified fabricated or inauthentic subscribers as a residual possibility. It missed the important benign-but-material alternative that the posting-time batch can distort downstream month-based retention or renewal analytics even when cash, entitlements, and source-event reconciliation are correct.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Explicitly compare posted_at with effective_event_date for all 17 rows, document the duplicate cash and entitlement reconciliation at row or source-event level, and recommend that downstream analytics use effective_event_date rather than treating the absence of a financial issue as absence of all operational impact.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "SOUTH region has severely high ABANDONED (648) and ERROR (558) IVR outcomes"
"685 SOUTH region IVR calls terminated at the `authenticate` stage (far higher than other regions)"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The fall in CareDesk complaint cases is not evidence of improved customer experience; it is a measurement artifact caused by customers abandoning calls or encountering errors at the authentication stage before a case can be generated."
"Cases fell because callers were blocked, not because they were satisfied."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "We do not know whether the authentication failure is due to a technical defect (system timing out/errors) or poor prompt UX confusing the customers."
"We also do not know if these abandoned callers are switching to other channels (like physical stores) or churning entirely."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not expand the pilot nationally yet."
"Has there been any independent follow-up on a sample of the unauthenticated dropped calls to verify if their underlying issues were actually resolved?"

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Safe Next Action: Halt the pilot expansion and analyze the technical pilot report to determine exactly why so many calls are terminating at the authentication stage."
"Are customers who fail authentication calling back repeatedly, and how are these repeat contacts captured if they aren't logged in CareDesk?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Complaint cases fell due to upstream funnel constraint, not resolution" is presented with High confidence, but the submission does not establish timing, a pre-pilot comparison, or linkage from failed IVR sessions to complaint outcomes.

"The fall in CareDesk complaint cases ... is a measurement artifact caused by customers abandoning calls or encountering errors at the authentication stage" overstates causality: the IVR counts support a capture-failure hypothesis, not proof that these events caused the case decline.

"Cases fell because callers were blocked, not because they were satisfied" incorrectly treats abandonment and authentication errors as sufficient evidence that affected callers were blocked and dissatisfied; abandonment is not itself a complaint or proof of customer harm.

"SOUTH region has severely high ABANDONED (648) and ERROR (558) IVR outcomes" lacks a cited comparison period or explicit regional denominators, so the magnitude and relevance of the claimed spike are not fully demonstrated.
The submission does not substantiate that the South-only case decline coincided with the pilot date or show that service-event exposure did not improve in parallel.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled technical-defect versus prompt-UX explanations and possible switching to other channels, but missed the strongest benign alternative: increased IVR abandonment may reflect a mixture of normal non-complaint callers and operational or service changes, so the logged abandonment/error population cannot by itself establish either dissatisfaction or the cause of the CareDesk decline.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Link IVR sessions to downstream journey outcomes, repeat contacts, and resolution across channels, supplemented by sampled call listening, while comparing pre/post South results and service-event exposure before asserting that the case decline was caused by capture failure.

dimensions.name: A. Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites `inverter_events.csv` for both the recovery event and the five-day gap.
It also refers to `impact_mw` being 0, `cleared=yes`, and low durations, but does not provide the specific INV-09 rows, timestamps, or field values.

dimensions.name: B. Investigative reasoning
citations: It tests plausible benign explanations for the missing precursor: “the pipeline dropped this critical event” or “the export query simply filtered it out.”
It rejects active equipment failure using the zero-impact, cleared, and short-duration evidence rather than treating event wording alone as proof.
It does not explicitly discuss whether a recovery event can legitimately appear without a precursor in the exported window or event-generation logic.

dimensions.name: C. Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission appropriately says event wording alone cannot establish failure and limits its recommendation to “one cheap check.”
It distinguishes the high-confidence observations from the inference that a preceding fault is missing.
Calling the absent precursor a “critical event” and treating the recovery as implying one is somewhat stronger than the supplied evidence establishes.

dimensions.name: D. Decision/action quality
citations: The proposed raw-database query is inexpensive and discriminates between an export/query omission and a broader logging defect.
The recommendation to stop if the raw event is present is proportionate and avoids unnecessary physical maintenance escalation.
The action could be better scoped by checking the event-definition/query window first, since a precursor may have occurred outside the exported period.

dimensions.name: E. Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion avoids inventing a plant problem from zero-MW, cleared, short-duration events and recommends stopping after a limited verification.
It is directionally consistent with the evidence, though it gives more prominence to the missing-originator check than necessary for an apparently harmless communications/event-quality anomaly.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “TEMP_SENSOR_RECOVERED ... implies a preceding fault state” is plausible but not proven without the event schema or state-machine definition.
Describing the absent precursor as a “critical event” is unsupported; the evidence shows an event-recording or export-quality question, not operational criticality.
“If it is missing from the raw database, escalate as a telemetry/logging defect” is reasonable but should distinguish a raw-database defect from an upstream event-generation or retention issue.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The recovery event may be validly present without a precursor in this export because the fault occurred before the export window, was not configured to be logged, or was filtered by event type/query logic. The observed zero MW impact, cleared status, and short duration support a benign transient rather than equipment failure.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: State the exact INV-09 recovery timestamp and event fields, then verify the export time window and event-definition/query filters before labeling the missing precursor a defect.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "May 28 and May 29 had different baseline weather and actual generation" — sourced to `dispatch_blocks.csv`.
"The 31.6% claim compares total penalties across these two different days" — sourced to `AI_Pilot_Impact_Note.md`.
"A counterfactual calculation for May 29 using `base_schedule_mw` yields a baseline penalty of ~Rs 549,664" and "The actual May 29 penalty is Rs 453,086" — both sourced to `dispatch_blocks.csv`.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: "the evidence does not support the note's 31.6% impact claim, as it relies on a flawed comparison between two different days with different wind conditions."
"compute the counterfactual `base_schedule_mw` penalty internally for every future pilot block".

The submission tests day-to-day weather and generation variation, but does not fully test whether `base_schedule_mw` is a valid causal counterfactual or whether other operational factors affected the penalty.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "We cannot causally establish whether this 17.6% improvement will generalize to other days or conditions."
"It is based on a single-day sample of only 12 pilot blocks."
"We also cannot establish if the pilot would have performed better or worse on a day with the exact wind profile of May 28."

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: "immediately correct the methodology to use counterfactual baseline scheduling for impact analysis."
"Do not expand the pilot widely until consistent, positive counterfactual performance is validated over multiple days."
The proposed future per-block comparison is a discriminating test and preserves a cautious operational posture rather than discarding the pilot entirely.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: "The evidence does not support the note's 31.6% impact claim" while retaining that May 29 performed better against its same-day base schedule.
"approximately 17.6% compared to what the penalty would have been using the conventional base schedule on that exact same day."
The conclusion correctly distinguishes the cross-day headline from the smaller same-day counterfactual benefit, although its causal wording is somewhat stronger than the design warrants.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The AI pilot successfully reduced the DSM penalty" and "This isolates the AI's impact" overstate what a same-day base-versus-submitted comparison establishes; it shows better performance relative to the base schedule, but does not by itself prove the pilot caused the difference.

"Over half the difference was due to natural day-to-day variance" is not fully demonstrated in the submission unless the underlying penalty decomposition and calculations are shown; the evidence supports confounding by different weather and generation, but not necessarily that precise attribution.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: May 29's submitted schedule performed better than the conventional base schedule under the observed conditions, but the roughly 17.6% difference is an estimated benchmark comparison rather than a fully identified causal effect. Differences in forecast inputs, operational constraints, or the validity of the base schedule could account for part of it.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Validate the `base_schedule_mw` counterfactual across multiple pre-specified pilot and non-pilot days, with block-level penalty decomposition and matched weather/generation conditions or randomized schedule assignment where operationally safe.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The first 6 digits (902110) correctly match the globally harmonized base code for this product" — sourced to `product_master_current.xlsx`, `declaration.pdf`.
"Switzerland is absent from the tariff matrix, causing the system to rely on a fallback master code" — sourced to `country_tariff_matrix.xlsx`.
"The automated check performs a literal 8-digit string match" — sourced to `canonical-schema-v0.3.md`, `review_note.txt`.
The submission identifies relevant files, but does not provide workbook rows, document excerpts, or the exact algorithm/configuration text.

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "Declaration Error (Wrong Product): Rejected because the declared code shares the exact HS6 root (`902110`) for P1001."
"Master Data is Universally Correct: Rejected because HS codes are only harmonized globally up to the first 6 digits."
"The official Swiss Customs Tariff schedule (Tares) for 9021.10" is explicitly identified as missing evidence.

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: The evidence table labels the country-specific-nomenclature and fallback explanations "High" confidence.
The decision states, "The code mismatch is a false positive," while also acknowledging that checking Tares would "definitively prove the broker's accuracy."

"Verifying that `90211000` is the correct 8-digit Swiss code ... would definitively prove the broker's accuracy" shows some uncertainty, but the headline conclusion and confidence ratings remain stronger than the unverified evidence supports.

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "The Swiss broker declared a locally valid 8-digit tariff code, while the automated flag compared it against an incompatible default 8-digit master code."
"Switzerland is absent from the tariff matrix, causing the system to rely on a fallback master code."

"configure the automated control to either compare only the first 6 digits (HS6) or maintain a proper country-specific tariff matrix for Switzerland" explains the likely data-lineage and control-design mechanism, though the submission does not quote the relevant configuration or matrix row.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Check `90211000` against the Swiss customs tariff database (Tares)."
"If valid, configure the automated control" to use HS6 or a country-specific matrix.
The recommendation is conditional, targeted, and avoids immediate escalation or irreversible changes before the Swiss tariff code is verified.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Do not escalate" and "The code mismatch is a false positive" are stated before the proposed Tares verification confirms the Swiss 8-digit code.
"The Swiss broker declared a locally valid 8-digit tariff code" is not established by the cited evidence as presented; the submission itself says Tares verification is still required.
"The 8th digit difference is due to country-specific tariff nomenclature" is asserted with high confidence without quoting the Swiss schedule or showing the relevant country-specific code mapping.
"The automated check performs a literal 8-digit string match" is plausible and cited to named files, but the submission provides no exact passage or rule identifier.

"If the broker had mistakenly declared a completely different product, the first 6 digits would not perfectly align" overstates the inference: an erroneous declaration can still share an HS6 category, and HS6 agreement alone does not prove the exact product or local 8-digit code.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The declaration may still contain an incorrect Swiss 8-digit code, or the product may be misclassified within the shared HS6 category. The HS6 match and absence of Switzerland from the matrix support a benign system mismatch, but they do not by themselves validate `90211000`; the Tares result and product-specific classification evidence are needed.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Perform and document the Tares lookup for the exact product and country, quoting the applicable Swiss tariff entry and the relevant rows/configuration showing the fallback and literal comparison before presenting the mismatch as definitively false positive.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "A preference claim (0.0% duty) was made on the declaration | `declaration.pdf`"
"Irish origin supplier document (SUP-02) expired on 2025-07-31 (before the Sept declaration) | `supplier_origin_register.csv`"
"The register may not be fully updated when sourcing routes change | `origin-workshop.md`"

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "The preference claim is definitively fraudulent: Rejected."
"The automated system should clear it based on ERP data: Rejected."
"we cannot definitively conclude fraud or permanent invalidity"

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "The available evidence is currently insufficient to support the preference claim."
"a valid, renewed supplier declaration for SUP-02 (Ireland) might exist offline"
"US-origin goods do not typically qualify for preferential duty into Ireland/EU."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "The register may not be fully updated when sourcing routes change"
"the register is \"not always updated\""
"ERP origin (US) actively contradicts a preference claim, and as explicitly noted in the workshop, ERP data is \"not for clearing a preference claim.\"

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Hold the preference claim."
"Request the procurement team to check their unindexed category folders for a renewed SUP-02 supplier declaration valid on 2025-09-18."
"Concurrently, ask the broker to formally clarify why US origin was declared alongside a preference claim."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "US-origin goods do not typically qualify for preferential duty into Ireland/EU" is a broad legal conclusion without identifying the applicable agreement, product-specific rules of origin, or whether the goods underwent qualifying processing.

"Declared origin and manufacturing country is the United States" risks conflating manufacturing country with preferential origin; manufacturing in the United States does not by itself resolve preferential origin.

"ERP origin (US) actively contradicts a preference claim" is overstated because an ERP manufacturing/origin field may be inaccurate, may refer to non-preferential origin, or may not capture qualifying processing and the applicable preference rules.

A renewed SUP-02 supplier declaration would be relevant evidence but would not alone establish preferential eligibility without confirming the goods, applicable rules of origin, and required proof and transaction coverage.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The goods may have been manufactured in the United States but acquired preferential origin through qualifying processing or another applicable rule, or the declaration's origin field may be erroneous or refer to a different origin concept. Separately, SUP-02 may reflect an outdated register rather than an invalid supplier document; these possibilities require the supplier, product, and applicable origin-rule evidence rather than inference from the Irish supplier route alone.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Explicitly separate manufacturing country, non-preferential origin, and preferential origin, then identify and request the product-specific rule of origin and complete supplier/broker proof covering the declaration date before concluding that the US data contradicts the preference claim.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The dataset maximum `qcore_release_ts` is July 22" — `batch_release.csv`
"The snapshot claims to represent July 31" — `source_freshness.csv`
"42 batches are unreleased (null), many with lab completions up to July 31" — `batch_release.csv`
"The 24-hour target relies on both lab and supplier certificate availability" — `qc_release_sop.md`

The claims identify relevant files and fields, but the submission does not cite specific rows or quantify the claimed concentration/timing pattern, and it treats the July 22 maximum as truncation without establishing that directly.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "Calculating a simple average over the available timestamps ignores survivorship bias"
"It also fails to filter out `open_deviation = True` cases"

The submission tests survivorship and SOP eligibility, but does not investigate whether release timestamps are interface commits rather than decision times, does not profile the extreme 02:10 concentration, and does not test whether the extracts are a coherent snapshot.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "Confidence" is marked "High" for the July 22 maximum and July 31 snapshot mismatch.
"The 'day and a half' average duration is a misleading and unusable KPI"

The evidence supports a freshness mismatch and missing certificate timing, but high confidence that the dataset is "artificially" censored and the categorical "unusable" conclusion are stronger than the demonstrated evidence.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "A refreshed dataset with a valid QCore join up to July 31, and the inclusion of a `certificate_received_ts` field"

The recommendation appropriately challenges use of the KPI and requests a better snapshot, but it does not propose a small reversible validation, define success criteria, or protect against optimizing an interface-timestamp artifact.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "The 'day and a half' average accurately reflects routine QC performance: Rejected"
"It also fails to filter out `open_deviation = True` cases"

The submission gives some rationale for rejecting routine-performance interpretation, but does not actively test the strongest competing explanation: that apparent delay is caused by timestamp semantics or extract misalignment rather than workflow delay.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "A refreshed dataset with a valid QCore join up to July 31"
"the inclusion of a `certificate_received_ts` (COA arrival time) field"

These are relevant requests, but they are not prioritized by decision value and omit the highest-value request for the event/decision timestamp definition or raw event log needed to distinguish workflow delay from interface timing.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The QCore release dataset abruptly truncates on July 22, artificially censoring 9 days of recent releases" — the maximum timestamp and freshness mismatch establish an inconsistency, not by themselves deliberate or mechanical truncation.
"The 'day and a half' average duration is ... unusable" — it may be unusable for the stated KPI decision, but the submission does not test timestamp semantics or quantify the impact of the mismatch.

"The KPI start condition relies solely on `lab_complete_ts`" — this is not reconciled with the SOP wording that the target starts when required evidence is available; the missing certificate timestamp demonstrates measurement inability, not necessarily that the implemented clock explicitly starts at lab completion alone.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The apparent long cycle time may primarily reflect QCore interface-commit timestamps, especially given the extreme concentration of releases around 02:10, and/or non-coherent extract snapshots. Workflow delay and missing certificate timing remain viable, but the submission does not distinguish them.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Request the timestamp definitions and a raw event sample containing evidence-availability, decision/approval, and QCore release events, joined to a single as-of snapshot; use it to quantify how much of the apparent cycle time is workflow delay versus interface timing before declaring the KPI unusable.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "MaintStar-global inventory quantity snapshot is over a month old (June 26)" — `source_freshness.csv`; "Local reservations/critical status were updated recently (July 30)" — `part_restrictions.csv`; "the highest-value requests (e.g. PR-260700 servo drives at $21,751)" — `part_requests.csv`, `spare_parts.csv`.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "Finding identically described or synonymous parts is only the first hurdle. Strict business rules (critical-asset reservations, revision letters, site qualifications) disqualify 71.1% of the value." This separates semantic retrieval from transferability and identifies several operational mechanisms, but does not show the row-level tests or fully address manufacturer part number, UOM, and temporal join risks.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission distinguishes "Actionable Now," "Needs Engineering Check," and "Not Transferable from Current Evidence," and states: "Because the MaintStar-global snapshot is from June 26, the global quantity data is stale." This is useful claim-specific uncertainty, although the precise bounds for the three categories and the residual uncertainty in the Actionable Now group are not shown.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "The semantic-search pilot successfully identifies compatible parts across varying catalog descriptions, but the true opportunity is much smaller than the raw matches suggest." The recommendation to obtain "a live physical count or live CMMS integration" before executing transfers is operationally protective, but it lacks a small reversible test, explicit success criteria, and a clear engineering/availability confirmation workflow for candidate generation.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "All semantic matches are immediately transferable: Rejected." The servo-drive example tests one important competing hypothesis using reservation and revision evidence, but alternatives such as stale data causing false negatives or inability to prove transferability rather than actual non-transferability are not actively tested.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "A live physical count or live CMMS integration for `available_qty_global`" is a relevant request and recognizes the stale source, but it presents two relatively broad options without prioritizing the smallest high-value query or specifying which candidate transfers should be checked first.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Strict business rules ... disqualify 71.1% of the value" is stronger than the evidence presented: the submission does not show the row-level restriction, revision, qualification, reservation, UOM, or manufacturer-part-number checks supporting every item in that percentage.

The label "Actionable now" may be overstated while the only global inventory quantity snapshot is from June 26; current stock, reservation state, and transferability should be confirmed before treating those matches as executable.

"The true opportunity is much smaller" is directionally plausible from the classification table, but the calculation and treatment of candidate value versus actionable value are not independently auditable from the submission alone.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 71.1% classified as Not Transferable may partly represent not-yet-provable transferability rather than actual incompatibility. A current inventory and restriction extract, joined by manufacturer part number and validated for revision, UOM, qualification, reservation, and criticality, could convert some apparent negatives into actionable candidates; conversely, stale quantities could also invalidate some current positives.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide a row-level audit for every candidate, starting with the highest-value requests and the eight Actionable Now items, joining request and stock by manufacturer part number and explicitly recording revision, UOM, qualification, reservation/criticality, site, quantity, and source timestamp; then reclassify candidates using a live or freshly reconciled stock check before any transfer.
